value.title: Canonical problem
value.currentStateSummary: A finite-block code-induced dependence-balance condition and compatible rate inequalities are established. An exact finite entropic witness also shows that the specified entropy-only and finite copy-lemma relaxation cannot improve the classical UV value. These results constrain converse strategies but do not change the certified capacity frontier or numerical upper bound.

value.title: Code-induced dependence balance and entropy/copy no-go theorem
scopeQualifications: The finite-block necessary condition applies to deterministic private-message codes on finite-alphabet memoryless two-receiver broadcast channels and hence to the BSSC; reliable bounded-rate sequences make its dependence-balance defect vanish.
The alphabets of U, V, and W may grow with blocklength, so the condition is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region or a certified numerical capacity bound.

The no-go theorem concerns only the precisely stated entropy/copy relaxation at uniform input; it does not preclude binary-BSSC posterior constraints, jointly consistent channel-specific refinements, or direct code inequalities.
The entropic witness is not generated by a binary BSSC: its X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components, and exact binary-posterior consistency excludes it.
No achievability result, capacity formula, global converse optimum, or improvement over the existing certified BSSC upper bound follows.

proofs: Define Di=I(A;B|Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n). Each balance summand is Di-D_{i-1}, giving the exact telescope. Nonnegativity and separate Fano bounds control the two endpoints and yield the absolute defect bound after time sharing.

Conditioning on (A,B,T) fixes the current input, while channel memorylessness separates the current output pair from the past/future state W. Chain rules and conditioned Csiszar sum identities give the four rate rows without an unproved sign assumption.

For the no-go theorem, a calculus argument gives the sharp scalar BSSC support value r=h2(1/4)-3/4. An explicit tuple construction from independent binary components realizes all required entropy, structural, dependence-balance, conditional BEC, and support constraints and attains both objective branches exactly.

Every standard copy step is realizable by conditional resampling of the finite witness, preserving its original marginal and objective; universal finite-variable information inequalities also hold because the witness is genuinely entropic.
methods: Finite-block telescoping, separate Fano endpoint control, time sharing with the encoder-coordinate map retained, and conditioned Csiszar identities.
Exact affine-in-h component-entropy construction and set-union/intersection evaluation of entropies and conditional mutual informations.
computations: The exact standard-library checker verify_exact_witness.py (SHA-256 0be3d1bf7dfc02f22cc55cd52fafcb7e9290cfb32db7d4a103a570deefb0f32b) verifies component positivity, the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, both zero dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both support rows, and both objective branches without floating-point arithmetic.
tools: Python 3 standard-library symbolic checker representing every entropy as a rational affine expression in h=h2(1/4) and evaluating tuple variables through independent-component set operations.

value.title: Code-induced BSSC converse structure
value.objective: Convert structural constraints inherited from reliable private-message codes into rigorous, optimizable BSSC converse bounds and identify refinements capable of improving the certified bound.
value.currentStateSummary: Every deterministic finite-block code induces an asymptotically exact dependence-balance relation, a fixed-coordinate encoder law, and four compatible rate inequalities. A finite entropic counterfeit proves that the specified universal entropy-inequality and finite copy-lemma refinement route cannot beat the classical UV value. The remaining viable directions require support reduction or genuinely channel-specific consistency information.
value.localResidualSummary: Prove a support or compactness reduction preserving the induced law and rate rows, certify any resulting global optimization, or derive exact jointly consistent binary-BSSC posterior constraints or direct multiletter inequalities that exclude the entropic counterfeit and strengthen the converse.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted claim is a dependency-complete structural converse result: its finite-block theorem supplies the code-induced constraints, while its entropic witness diagnoses the limits of one refinement route. Both components directly serve the durable objective of converting code structure into a stronger BSSC converse, so they are retained together as one reusable intermediate result in a dedicated child program.

topologyRationale: Create one objective-based child program to separate code-induced converse development from the undifferentiated canonical residual. No existing programs or results require movement, retirement, splitting, or merging.
